title: Annotatio V §.XII fifth: Sennertus — sacraments seals not fundamental/principal articles
pass_a_gloss: But that we may match the Author’s fivefold number of Proofs for Oral Eating’s Fundamentality with the number of Lutheran Testimonies against the same — indeed against the whole Sacrament of the Supper as numbered among faith’s Fundamental dogmas — come, let us now superadd one more to the four formerly brought forward, and indeed of a Professor not long since of Wittenberg, whose Authority with the Author will have been greater than Calixtus’s: It is the Testimony of ANDREAS SENNERT in his Theological Exercise on the fundamental articles of faith §. LXIV, to be read in these words: The Sacraments follow, and indeed those first considered in genus or common. That we have referred them neither to FUNDAMENTAL ARTICLES OF FAITH NOR PRINCIPAL ones, no one will easily marvel … if he consider with us (1) that the Apostle Rom. 4:11 names them seals, seals of faith, and so notably distinguishes them from the Substance or Substantial things of faith. And certainly (2) by their nature they do not so much generate or produce faith (outside the initiation sacrament) as (3) after the nature of seals in contracts, covenant, testaments, they confirm and increase faith as certain external visible Symbols. Whence (4) … (5) they are Necessary by reason of the Institutor and force of divine mandate: (6) BUT NOT SIMPLY OR ABSOLUTELY FOR FAITH OR SALVATION, which could be proved by Holy Scripture’s sayings and examples.
pass_b_english: To match the Author’s five proofs, Strimesius adds a fifth Lutheran witness — Wittenberg’s Andreas Sennert (§.LXIV), whose weight with the Author tops Calixtus.

Sennert: sacraments (as a class) are neither fundamental nor principal faith articles — Paul calls them seals of faith (Rom 4:11), distinct from faith’s substance; they confirm faith like contract seals; necessary by mandate, but not simply or absolutely for faith or salvation.
source_text: Ceterum ut numero Probationum quinario Autoris, quô pro Fundamentalitate Oralis Manducationis, depugnavit, Numerum Testimoniorum Lutheranorum contra eandem, quin totum Sacramentum Cœnæ, quatenus Fundamentalibus fidei dogmatibus annumeratur, adæquemus, agedum adhuc unum, in medium olim allatis quatuor, nunc superaddemus, & quidem cujusdam Professoris, non ita pridem Wittebergensis, cujus Auctoritas apud Autorem major fuerit, quàm Calixti: Est verò Testimonium ANDREÆ SENNERTI in Exercitat. ejus Theologica de Articulis fidei fundamentalibus §. LXIV. his verbis legendum: Sacramenta succedunt, & quidem illa in genere vel communi primùm considerata. Quæ, quòd neque ad ARTICULOS FIDEI FUNDAMENTALES, NEQUE PRINCIPALES, retulimus, nemo mirabitur facilè (utut in re majoris momenti nemini vicissim præjudicamus) si consideret nobiscum, (1) quod Apostolus Rom. IV, 11. eadem signacula, sigilla fidei nominet; adeoque hoc ipso à Substantia vel Substantialibus fidei notanter distinguat. Et certè (2) per naturam suam fidem non tam (extra initiationis sacr.) ingenerant aut producunt: quàm (3) qua sigillorum in contractibus, fœdere, testamentis, natura aut ratio vel conditio est, Symbola tanquam quædam certa, externa & visibilia, fidem confirmant adaugentque. Unde (4) cùm in Vet. & Novo Testamento, Substantialia eadem & una sint … sigilla gratiæ tamen sunt fueréque diversa … adeoque (5) Necessaria, quidem sunt ratione Instituentis, & vi mandati divini: (6) SED NON SIMPLICITER VEL ABSOLUTE AD FIDEM VEL SALUTEM, quod & dictis & exemplis Scripturæ S. poterat probari.
